subject: Follow-up: performance targets + context/window constraints for HelioHealth POC
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Qureshi <samira@heliohealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-17T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Quick recap + clarifying questions from today's perf discussion

Samira — thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap from our side and a few clarifying points so we can size a realistic POC/canary: 

Summary of what we heard:
- Use case: clinician-facing summarization & decision support during patient consults (retrieval + prompt composition).
- Desired user experience: near-realtime responses with progressive updates (streaming preferred).
- Typical session shape: long context (patient record + visit history) + short interactive prompts.

Clarifying items we need to finalize sizing:
1) Peak concurrency and burst profile — you mentioned ~150 concurrent active sessions typical and occasional spikes; could you confirm typical 95th/99th percentiles for concurrent active users and peak RPS (requests per second)?
2) Token envelope — what's the maximum practical input context (combined retrieved material + prompt) you expect to push into the model for the POC? We discussed 16k and 32k windows; please confirm which of these (or a different number) we should assume. Also confirm expected max generation length (output tokens) per request.
3) Latency target — you said clinician-facing responses should 'feel immediate'. Can you confirm a p95/p99 latency target (e.g., p95 < 800ms, p99 < 1.5s) and whether that applies to full response completion or to first token via streaming?
4) Streaming needs — do you require token-by-token streaming (SSE/WebSocket) for the main UX, or is chunked streaming acceptable?
5) Data residency/compliance — anything affecting where canary runs must be hosted?

Proposed immediate deliverables from Redwood:
- Baseline perf run using a Redwood-verified 32k-capable model with a streaming canary.
- Experimental configs: (A) dedicated reserved pool with KV cache + prefix extraction, (B) hosted autoscaled pool with aggressive batching and summarization pre-processing.
- Canary plan and instrumentation (we'll capture per-token latency, queueing, memory pressure, and fallback path behaviors).

Attachments: sample session CSV you mentioned would be great — can you share one export of ~50 sessions so we can model token distributions?

Next steps: once you confirm items 1–4 above we'll share the canary plan and a proposed schedule (aiming for a 7–10 day smoke + 3 day load window).

Thanks — Connor
Connor O'Brien | Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_canary_plan.docx (docx)]

From: Samira Qureshi <samira@heliohealth.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ops Team <ops@heliohealth.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-17T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap + clarifying questions from today's perf discussion

Connor — thanks for the concise recap. Confirming details below based on internal data and product expectations: 

1) Concurrency / bursts: typical active concurrent clinicians: 120–160 (varies by clinic).
   - 95th percentile concurrent: ~180
   - Burst scenario (e.g., morning shift change / outage failover): up to ~320 for ~2–5 minutes.
   - Typical RPS per clinic cluster: 15–30 req/s, aggregate spikes can reach 120 req/s.
2) Token envelope: for POC please model up to 24k combined input tokens (retrieved docs + current prompt). Output generation: usually 200–800 tokens; worst-case 1,600 tokens for long summaries.
3) Latency targets: priority is clinician productivity so we want p95 perceived latency < 950ms for the first useful token via streaming, and full completion p95 < 2.5s if possible for <800-token outputs. p99 targets are softer for this trial (p99 < 4s).
4) Streaming: token-by-token (SSE/WebSocket) is our preferred UX for partial results. Chunked streaming is acceptable as a fallback but prefer lower-latency incremental tokens.
5) Data residency: US-only for the POC; we can use a dedicated region.

I've attached a small sample (helio_session_samples.csv) showing token distributions and a few long-session exports. Also attached is our standard MSA snippet for trial terms. 

We'll prioritize a canary in your hosted US region first. Please propose a timeline and we can lock a 2-week window next month.

—Samira
Samira Qureshi | Director, Product Ops — HelioHealth
[Attachment: helio_session_samples.csv (csv)] [Attachment: ms-terms-draft.pdf (pdf)]

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Qureshi <samira@heliohealth.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-17T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick recap + clarifying questions from today's perf discussion — initial sizing notes

Samira / Connor — thanks for the data, the CSV was helpful. High-level notes from a solutions sizing perspective and tradeoffs we propose for the POC: 

Observations from helio_session_samples.csv:
- Median combined context ~3.2k tokens, mean ~6.8k, tail to ~22k on ~4% of sessions.
- Generation length: median ~320 tokens, mean ~540, tail up to ~1.4k.

Implications & recommended config options:
A) Streaming-first canary (fastest perceived latency)
   - Use a 32k-capable encoder/decoder variant or chunked retrieval + semantic ranker to limit active prefix size when practical.
   - Token-by-token streaming implementation to ensure first-token p95 < 950ms. We estimate first-token time ~250–600ms depending on active context size and KV cache hits.
   - Cache: implement session-level KV caching for repeated retrievals (recent documents), expect 30–60% reduction in average context size for follow-up prompts.

B) Dedicated-reserved pool for predictable p95/p99
   - Reserve a small fleet (N GPUs tuned for long-context servicing). Avoid preemptible instances for p99 guarantees.
   - Autoscaling policy: maintain headroom for 320-connection 2–5 min bursts by allowing short-term burst buffer (burst nodes or serverless-style warm pool).

C) Fallbacks and hedging
   - For extremely large contexts (tail >20k): two-tier strategy — (1) run a fast summarizer to compress long documents before full generation; (2) automatically degrade to chunked answer with a clear UX indicator.
   - Hedging: for latency-critical prompts we can issue a shallow fast model + deeper long-model and return the fast answer first, then patch if needed. Adds cost but improves p95.

Instrumentation & success criteria for the POC:
- Track: first-token latency, completion latency, per-token generation time, queueing time, GPU memory high-water marks, and cache hit rate.
- Goal: achieve first-token p95 < 950ms (streaming) and completion p95 < 2.5s for outputs <800 tokens on the dedicated path.

Proposed next steps (action items):
1) Redwood: produce a 7–10 day canary plan (configuration A + B), with specific test harness and success metrics — deliverable by 2026-10-20. [redwood_canary_plan.docx attached].
2) HelioHealth: confirm preferred 2-week window in November or the week of 2026-11-09 and provide a single point of contact for test orchestration.
3) Contracting: Connor to coordinate trial MSA review — see ms-terms-draft.pdf attached; Laura to provide estimated reserved capacity cost ballpark for review.

I'll run a quick perf estimate tonight and share numbers (RPS -> GPU count) before EOD tomorrow. 

—Laura
Laura Bennett | Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_canary_plan.docx (docx)]

Connor
